questions.q: What does the Edit Title dialog default to?
options: A <Sheet Name> placeholder that shows the worksheet's own name
A completely blank title with no default text
The name of the data source
The workbook's file name
questions.explain: Every worksheet's title defaults to a <Sheet Name> placeholder, which you can rewrite, reformat, or replace.

questions.q: What does Tableau's auto-generated caption describe?
options: Which fields are on which shelves and which filters are currently active, in plain sentences
The exact SQL query sent to the data source
A list of every user who has viewed the workbook
The workbook's file size
questions.explain: The default caption is generated automatically from the view's structure — its fields, shelves, and active filters — written out as plain text.

questions.q: What does a reference line do?
options: Adds a fixed or computed value (like an average) directly onto the chart for instant comparison
Deletes marks that fall below a certain value
Changes the chart's mark type
Filters the underlying data source
questions.explain: A reference line draws a computed or constant value across the view so every mark can be compared against it visually.

questions.q: What is an annotation attached to?
options: One specific mark, point, or area in the view
The entire workbook, regardless of which sheet is active
Only map visualizations
The Data pane
questions.explain: Annotations are callouts tied to a specific mark, point, or area — not a global, workbook-wide element.

questions.q: How do you add an annotation to a mark?
options: Right-click the mark and choose Annotate
Drag a field onto the Annotations shelf
Open the Extract dialog and select Annotate
Annotations can only be added through a calculated field
questions.explain: Right-clicking a mark, point, or area and selecting Annotate opens the annotation editor for that specific spot in the view.
